taxonomyNote: NatureServe spells it 'Mearns's Rock Lizard' (alt. 'Banded Rock Lizard'); the California agency account spells 'Mearn's'. NatureServe notes Grismer (1999) treated P. mearnsi and P. slevini as separate species and that northern and southern clades exist within P. mearnsi.
behavior: Diurnal; shuttles between sun and shade, active all day even in hot weather, from about mid-March to late summer.
Forages on vertical and under-rock surfaces; eats beetles, ants, bees, flies, spiders and some buds and blossoms.
Males defend territories (tolerating subadult males); females defend against other females; home ranges about 85 m2 (males) and 40 m2 (females) in one study.
habitat: Most abundant among massive rocks: cliffs, boulder piles and canyon walls in shaded, narrow parts of desert-slope canyons, and desert washes and palm oases.
Rarely found on open ground; shelters in rock cracks and crevices.
range: From San Gorgonio Pass (Riverside County, California) south through the Peninsular Ranges to at least Bahia de los Angeles in Baja California, plus some Gulf of California islands; in the US limited to eastern San Diego and central Riverside counties, to about 1,200 m.
